title: Korean Fried Chicken
subtitle: Crispy double-fried chicken in a sticky gochujang glaze
excerpt: The revolutionary Korean fried chicken technique: double-frying wings and pieces at two different temperatures to produce an extraordinarily crisp, thin crust with juicy meat inside, glazed in a sweet, spicy gochujang sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Korean fried chicken (chikin) emerged as a distinct style in South Korea in the 1970s and became internationally celebrated from the 2000s onwards, particularly after featuring in Bon Appetit and various food media as a revelatory fried chicken technique. The defining innovation is double-frying: the chicken is fried first at a lower temperature (around 150 to 160 C) to cook through without browning, then fried again at a higher temperature (175 to 180 C) to develop an extremely crisp, thin, almost glassy crust. The crust is typically made with potato starch or cornflour rather than breadcrumbs, producing a different texture. The yangnyeom (sauce) version, glazed in gochujang, is the most internationally famous.

recipeTools.notes: A deep, heavy pan for frying.

content.text: Double-frying is the key. First fry at 155 C for 8 minutes to cook through; remove, rest for 5 minutes, then fry again at 180 C for 3 to 4 minutes to crisp. The rest between fries is essential: it allows the steam inside the crust to escape so the second fry produces maximum crunch. Apply the sauce immediately before serving; sauced chicken softens quickly.

items.preparation: bone-in wings and thighs, or boneless thighs cut into 4 cm pieces

content.text: Mix the cornflour, plain flour, baking powder, and salt. Toss the chicken pieces in this mixture, pressing firmly so the dry coating adheres. Shake off any excess. Heat the oil to 155 C in a deep, heavy pan.

First fry: add the chicken in batches and fry at 155 to 160 C for 8 to 9 minutes until cooked through but not yet deeply coloured. Remove and rest on a rack for 5 minutes. Increase the oil temperature to 180 C. Second fry: fry the chicken again for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden and very crisp.

Make the sauce: combine the gochujang, honey, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger in a small pan and warm over medium heat, stirring, for 2 minutes. Toss the hot chicken in the sauce to coat thoroughly. Transfer to a plate, scatter with sesame seeds and spring onion. Serve immediately.
